speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. How old are you, and when did you or your family first notice that your blood pressure might be high? Have you been experiencing any headaches, dizziness, or shortness of breath lately?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: I am surprised to hear his blood pressure is elevated since he seems well; can you tell me if you've noticed any swelling in his legs or if he seems unusually tired or short of breath during play? Also, has he had any recent abdominal pain or changes in his urination?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text: Doctor: That is an unusual finding; could you clarify if the high blood pressure was measured in both arms, or if the reading was significantly higher in the right arm compared to the left? I would also like to check if there is a pulse in his right wrist and foot to compare them.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text: Doctor: Since the elevated reading was isolated to the right arm, I need to confirm if his blood pressure is normal in the left arm and if his femoral pulses are strong and equal to his brachial pulses. This discrepancy often suggests a vascular issue like Coarctation of the Aorta, so I will now perform a cardiovascular examination to listen for murmurs and check pulse symmetry. REQUEST TEST: Blood Pressure_Bilateral_Arms REQUEST TEST: Blood Pressure_Legs REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Pressure Right Upper Extremity: 150/80 mm Hg; Blood Pressure Legs: Lower values compared to upper extremities; Pulses: 2+ radial pulses and trace femoral pulses; Heart Auscultation: Normal S1 and S2, 2/6 long systolic murmur with systolic ejection click over the left sternal border and back; Chest X-ray: Normal heart size, rib notching not observed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Doctor: Given the significant blood pressure difference between the arms and legs, along with weak femoral pulses and a systolic ejection click, I suspect a congenital narrowing of the aorta. To confirm the diagnosis and visualize the extent of the narrowing, I will request an echocardiogram. REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Echocardiogram Findings: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta
